title: A Divine Chariot and Weapons Descend for Krishna
story:
Mathura was ringed by the greatest army the age had seen. Jarasandha of Magadha had come with twenty-three divisions to avenge Kamsa, the tyrant king of Mathura whom the brothers Krishna and Balarama had struck down, and he had sworn that no Yadava would be left alive beneath the sun. Day and night the fires of the besiegers ringed the walls.

Krishna stood looking out at the host, and while he looked, he thought. These warring kings lay heavy on the earth; this gathering itself was another weight laid upon her. "I will destroy this force," he said within himself, "this weight heaped on the earth. It was to lift such burdens that I came down, and while I do this work, another part of me is ever at work, keeping what is right safe in the world." And as he finished the thought, the sky answered him.

Out of the empty air above Mathura two chariots descended, bright as the sun itself. Each had its driver at the reins, and each carried the ancient weapons of a warrior, bows, quivers, maces, armor, things old beyond memory yet gleaming as though made that morning. No one had sent them and no one had summoned them. They came of their own accord, sinking down out of the light like the answer to a question not yet spoken, and came to rest before the two brothers.

Krishna turned to Balarama. "Look, brother," he said. "Calamity has come upon the Yadavas, and they look to you. It was for this that we two were born, to bring ease to the good."

The brothers armed themselves, and the ancient weapons fitted them as if they had been shaped for them all along. Then the two chariots rolled out through the gates of Mathura, past the citizens who had come running into the streets, and out onto the open ground between the walls and the enemy host.

Krishna's chariot was driven by Daruka, his charioteer. As the wheels cleared the gate, Krishna raised to his lips the great conch at his side and blew it once. The sound rolled across the plain like thunder walking the earth, deep and unhurried, filling the whole space between the city and the camps.

In the tents of the Magadha king, in the ranks of the allied kings, in the hearts of the soldiers who had come to wipe the Yadavas from the face of the earth, terror entered and took hold. Men looked at one another and did not know why their hands trembled.

Two chariots stood before the greatest army the age had seen, and for a moment the army did not move. The sun stood high over Mathura. The conch's echo went on fading over the fields.

Then the battle began.
reflection: The chariots come down of their own accord, at the exact moment Krishna resolves to act — as if heaven had been waiting for his decision. His weighing of the earth's burden is described in wholly human terms, and the divine answer arrives only when the human resolve is complete.
next_story_tease: Jarasandha's host rolled forward to meet the two chariots, and the greatest battle of the age began.
hero_scene: Two sun-bright chariots descending out of the sky over Mathura, their drivers holding ancient divine weapons, while Krishna and Balarama below look up at the falling light; beyond the walls, the vast enemy camp darkens the plain to the horizon.

the gates and walls of Mathura
